reply_markdown:
## 1. Prior findings (F29/F30/F32)

All F29-1..2, F30-1..4/6..9 and F32-1..11 are **fixed** in `1de388e`. The F02/F03/F04/F15/F19-1/F22-6 series predate this range (panel/routing/ratings/scoreboard code marked `implemented` at `c6f6966`) and were **not re-checked** in this wave-28 pass.

- **Kick (D1)** `common.ps1:8377-8415`, `consult.ps1:1257-1273`: per-request id, atomic temp+rename, joiner takes the existing id and never overwrites, only the creator removes the ack after a 1 s grace, `Clear-StaleKickAck` sweeps >60 s acks. F29-2/F30-1/F32-1/F30-6 fixed.
- **Transactional hide (D3/D4)** `common.ps1:5562-5624`: snapshot, remove in `try`, restore+rethrow; engine start refuses on hide failure. F30-2/F30-4 fixed.
- **Bounded reader (D5)** `common.ps1:8416-8477`: only new bytes scanned, carry capped 1 MiB, multibyte split safe. F30-3/F32-8 fixed.
- **Health retry (D8)** `consult.ps1:5711-5753`: in-lock 1x1 s, full retry after the lock, cause named. F29-1/F30-7/F32-2/F32-3 fixed (residual #1).
- **Coordinator (D9-D12)** `common.ps1:5654-5846`: resolved triple, `in_roster:false`+console line, `#n` becomes a warning not a refusal, shared identity rule, weaker provider warning. F30-8/F30-9/F32-4/F32-5/F32-6 fixed.
- **Hook/`-Explain` (D13/D15)** `hook.ps1:113-115`, `consult.ps1:887-898`: full path, `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` substituted, stream disposed. F32-9/F32-11 fixed.
- **Test gate (D14)** `common.ps1:280-287`: hooks honoured only with `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_MODE=1`. F32-10 fixed.
- **Confirmed kill (D16)** `common.ps1:8652-8710`. Fixed (residuals #2/#3).

**F30-5 (docs vs code):** the `-Kick` caller text `consult.ps1:1274-1278` matches the code - "late"=outcome stands, "stopped"=salvaged, first reply stands. Consistent.

## 2. New defects / verification

**Telemetry is clean** (verified in code): `ConvertTo-TelemetryDetails` `common.ps1:9001-9046` emits only closed enums (engine/purpose/outcome), charset-constrained provider/model that reject path/drive shapes, and numeric counts/booleans/versions; `title`=outcome enum, `tags`=[engine,provider]; no path/task/prompt/thread/user/machine. `instance_id`=SHA-256(salt+machine name) `8902-8937`, name never in clear. One function `Get-TelemetrySwitch` is read identically by run/member/hook/sender (fail-closed). `-Complain` sends operator-typed text by design (shown + confirmed).

New findings (all minor/note, in `findings[]`):
1. Ledger records the in-lock health failure + "retried after it" but not the after-lock outcome; a crash between commit (`5725`) and retry (`5750`) loses the record while the ledger claims a retry.
2. Descendant kill-probe uses bare `Get-Process -Id` (`8685`), no start-time match - a recycled pid is a false survivor.
3. Non-Windows without `pgrep` - `Denied`, no `ps`/`/proc` fallback (`8293-8295`) - every timeout kill unconfirmed, continuation silently off.
4. `CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY_URL` + its loopback-http allowance are not test-gated (`8880-8892`) - a leftover harness value redirects real events.
5. `-Complain`'s spooled fallback re-serializes `-Compress` (`9487`) which differs from the pretty JSON shown (`9470-9472`).
6. A telemetry event can drop under 4-member spool contention with only `Write-Verbose` (`5762`).

**Documentation (verified):** README "Waiting: keep the prompt cache or compact" is arithmetically correct. Recomputed: Fable 1M one-wake 0.285 to 0.29, compact 1.75, boundary 1.5/0.285=5.3 wakes=2.6 h, expire 20; Fable 850K 0.2475 to 0.25 / 1.71 / 17; Opus 1M 1.4 h; Sonnet 1M 0.7 h; cold-resume cells 80/40/20 reads = 40/20/10 h. All match. Host sections use documented placeholders (`<clone>`,`$P`,`<zcode>`,`<name>`) + headless/`-Detach` guidance; **no command that cannot work as written** (Qwen/OpenCode/Muse flagged "not run live" - inferred).

## 3. Verdict

**ACCEPT.** No blocker or major remains: the telemetry leaving the machine is allowlisted and salted, every F29/F30/F32 item is fixed, and both named kick edge cases fail safe (id-less older caller gives a clean refusal/cleanup; dead creator still lets the joiner ack, 60 s sweep). The six residuals are minor/note (observability + narrow platform/whitespace edges) and can land in 28b.

findings.claim: The machine-wide-health retry records its intent durably but never its final outcome: when the in-lock retry fails, the ledger entry warning at 5718 permanently says 'retried after it', yet the after-lock retry runs at 5750 and its result (success or the real cause) is printed only to the transient console at 5751. A crash between Complete-StoreCommit (5725) and the after-lock retry (5750) loses the cross-repository health record while the committed ledger claims a retry happened, so a later forensic read of the ledger cannot tell that the record was ultimately lost.
findings.trigger: A run whose machine-health update fails, then the bridge process is killed (or crashes) after the ledger commit but before the after-lock retry completes; or the after-lock retry succeeds and the ledger still reads 'retried after it' with no recorded final state.

evidence.observation: 5718 adds 'machine-wide health not updated at the commit ($machineHealthCause); retried after it' to entry.warnings and 5719/5723-5725 commit it; the after-lock retry at 5749-5752 sets only $machineHealthLine (console), never writing the final outcome back to the committed ledger.

findings.verification: With fakes, force the in-lock machine-health attempt to fail, kill the bridge right after Complete-StoreCommit, then read the task ledger: the warning says 'retried after it' although no retry ran and the health file holds no record.
findings.remedy: After the after-lock retry, append its terminal result (delivered, or the cause) to the ledger entry or a small sidecar the next run reconciles, so the durable record reflects whether the cross-repository health write ultimately succeeded.

findings.claim: Stop-ProcessTreeChecked's descendant liveness probe uses bare `Get-Process -Id $d` with no start-time comparison, unlike the root which uses the handle-based `$Process.HasExited`. A descendant pid recycled by the OS to an unrelated process inside the 3-second poll window is counted as a survivor, so `$res.Confirmed` becomes false, `kill_confirmed` is false, the recovery state is 'survivors' and the task is wedged until the unrelated pid exits.
findings.trigger: A timeout kill of a process tree on a host under heavy process churn where one descendant pid is reused within ~3 s of the kill.

evidence.observation: 8682 uses $Process.HasExited for the root (immune to reuse) but 8685 tests descendants with Get-Process -Id $d only; 8707 sets Confirmed=false when any $alive remains; Get-DescendantTree returns only .Pids (8281/8316), no start times, so the probe cannot distinguish a recycled pid.

findings.verification: With fakes, kill a tree then start an unrelated process reusing a descendant pid inside the poll window and confirm kill_confirmed=false with a 'survivors' recovery state despite the original child being gone.
findings.remedy: Capture each descendant's start time in Get-DescendantTree and probe liveness with the existing start-time-aware Test-PidAlive/Test-RecordedProcess helper, as the root effectively does, so a recycled pid is not a false survivor.

findings.claim: On a non-Windows host without `pgrep`, Get-DescendantTree returns Denied='pgrep is not available' with no `ps` or `/proc` fallback, so Stop-ProcessTreeChecked cannot enumerate children and marks every timeout kill unconfirmed (Confirmed=false, 'the root exited, its children may not have'). Under D16 an unconfirmed kill means no continuation turn, so the documented timeout-continuation feature is silently disabled for that whole host class; the direction is safe and the warning names the cause, but the operator may not connect it to 'continuation is off'.
findings.trigger: A timeout kill on Linux in a minimal container (or any pwsh host) that has no `pgrep` binary.

evidence.observation: 8293-8295 sets Denied='pgrep is not available' and returns with no pids when not OnWindows and pgrep is absent (no ps/proc fallback); 8699-8704 then sets Confirmed=false because the children could not be enumerated.

findings.verification: On a Linux host with pgrep removed, force a timeout kill and confirm kill_confirmed=false and that no continuation turn runs although the root exited cleanly.
findings.remedy: When pgrep is absent, fall back to `ps -o pid=,ppid=` or parsing `/proc/*/stat` PPid to enumerate descendants, so enumeration (and therefore continuation) still works on hosts that have `ps`/`/proc` but not `pgrep`.

findings.claim: Get-TelemetryUrl reads CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY_URL directly from the environment and is not gated by CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_MODE, and its plain-http allowance for a loopback intake is likewise ungated - unlike the CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_* hooks which Get-TestHookValue ignores without test mode. A harness value left in a coordinator's shell therefore silently redirects real telemetry (including over http to a local intake) with no test-mode refusal; it is observable only via the notice/-Status Source string.
findings.trigger: A prior test run exports CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/T in the shell the coordinator later uses for a real consultation.

evidence.observation: 8880 reads CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY_URL straight from [Environment]; 8889 permits http when IsLoopback; Get-TestHookValue (283-287) returns '' unless Test-TestMode, and CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY_URL is not a TEST_ name so Get-IgnoredTestHooks does not warn it.

findings.verification: Export CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY_URL to a loopback http URL with no test mode, run a fake commit, and confirm the event is redirected there with only the -Status Source revealing it.
findings.remedy: Gate the plain-http loopback allowance on CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_MODE (real runs require https), and document CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY_URL as a production override whose Source is surfaced in the once-per-version notice.

findings.claim: -Complain tells the operator 'exactly this JSON goes to <url>' and shows the pretty `ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6` string, which the immediate send posts verbatim, but the spool fallback re-serializes the same payload with `-Compress`. The deferred/sender-delivered bytes are therefore not byte-for-byte what was shown (whitespace differs); field values are identical and allowlisted, so there is no privacy impact, only a mismatch with the literal claim.
findings.trigger: A -Complain whose immediate send fails (intake down / non-2xx) so the payload is kept in the spool and delivered later by the sender.

evidence.observation: 9470 builds pretty $json, 9471-9472 print it as 'exactly this JSON', 9481 sends $json verbatim, but 9487 spools `ConvertTo-Json -Compress -Depth 6 -InputObject $payload` - a whitespace-different re-serialization of the same object.

findings.verification: Force the immediate -Complain send to fail, then compare the shown pretty JSON with the spooled line: same fields, different whitespace.
findings.remedy: Spool the same $json string that was shown (it is already valid JSON) so shown==sent on both the immediate and the deferred path.

findings.claim: A telemetry event can be dropped when the spool file stays busy past the ~2 s exclusive-open retry under several panel members committing at once, and the drop is reported only through Write-Verbose, so there is no operator-visible counter. Telemetry is best-effort by design ('never fails the run'), so the impact is the loss of one allowlisted event plus no observability that it was lost.
findings.trigger: Four panel members finish and commit near-simultaneously on a slow volume, contending on the FileShare.None spool append.

evidence.observation: Submit-TelemetryEvent returns a $why string on spool failure (9172-9173) but the caller only does `if ($telemetryWhy) { Write-Verbose ... }` (5762); the spool append uses an exclusive open with a short retry (prior-verified Add-TelemetrySpoolLine/Open-TelemetrySpoolFile).

findings.verification: Hold the spool file open from a second process while four fake members commit and confirm at least one event is missing with no non-Verbose diagnostic.
findings.remedy: Track a dropped-event counter and surface it via codex-telemetry.ps1 -Status so lost telemetry is observable.

Health-update failures of any cause are retried and named: Update-MachineHealth sets MachineHealthLastError for a missing dir/lock timeout/write failure, the retry flag is set on any failure with the cause, one in-lock attempt at consult.ps1:5716 and the full retry after the lock at 5749-5753. Residual durability/observability gap filed as finding #1.
D1 kick protocol: per-request id, atomic write, joiner never overwrites, ack carries id+result, only the creator removes it, stale acks swept (common.ps1:8377-8415, consult.ps1:1257-1273).
Same D1 kick-id protocol resolves the concurrent-caller ack race: callers wait for their own id (consult.ps1:1261-1265), Clear-StaleKickAck sweeps >60 s acks (common.ps1:8395-8403).

D3: Hide-HostMarkers is transactional (snapshot, remove in try, restore+throw) and Start-EngineProcess refuses on a hide failure (common.ps1:5562-5594, ~1706-1709); confirmed against the D3 design comments at 5502-5512 and the prior-consultation read.

D5: Read-StreamChunk scans only new bytes and caps the carry at 1 MiB with oversized_lines counting (common.ps1:8416-8477, cap at 8426); multibyte split at a chunk boundary is safe because decoding runs on accumulated bytes.

D4: Remove-HostMarkersFromStartInfo returns a reason and verifies a clean environment; Start-ProbeProcess falls back to skipping the probe rather than starting it with markers (common.ps1:5605-5624); consistent with the prior-consultation read.

D1: Clear-StaleKickAck (common.ps1:8395-8403) removes an acknowledgement older than 60 s at -Kick start (consult.ps1:1225) and at run start (~4353), so a late ack after exit 3 no longer persists to the next same-number run.
Same fix as F29-1: every health-update failure (not only a lock timeout) is retried and the warning names the real cause (consult.ps1:5716-5718,5750-5751).

D9: a provider-label coordinator resolves to a single model when its roster entries name one model/engine, else the model stays null and Get-CoordinatorMatch returns 'provider' giving the weaker warning (common.ps1:5770-5773,5787-5799,5844); a model-less entry is no longer a provider-wide wildcard for the strong claim.

D10: Get-IdentityStringProblem shares the roster validator's character rule and allows interior blanks, refusing only empty/surrounding-blank/delimiter values (common.ps1:5677-5684), so a provider/model with interior spaces can be named in CODEX_CONSULT_COORDINATOR.

D1: concurrent -Kick callers no longer corrupt the ack - each request carries an id, a joiner takes the existing id and never overwrites, callers wait for their own id, only the creator removes the ack after a grace, stale acks are swept (common.ps1:8377-8415, consult.ps1:1257-1273).
D8: the in-lock machine-health retry is one attempt of at most 1 s (consult.ps1:5711-5716) so it cannot add 15 s to the write-lock hold; the full retry runs after Exit-StoreCommit (5745-5753).

Same fix as F29-1: a non-lock failure is retried and the warning names the actual cause rather than a hardcoded 'lock timeout' (consult.ps1:5716-5718,5750-5751). Residual: the durable ledger does not record the after-lock retry's final outcome - filed as finding #1.

D11: a label/lineage naming no roster entry is recorded with in_roster=false (common.ps1:5778) and shown as '(not in the roster - no reviewer can match it)' (5825) rather than refused, so a typo is surfaced, not silently disabling the guard.

D12: a '#n' naming no position yields Record.unresolved='#n' plus a warning and the run goes on (common.ps1:5753-5756); only an unparseable value is refused (5744-5746), so an operator-set #3 no longer breaks every run in a repository with a smaller/absent roster.

D9: a bare provider label gives the weaker 'provider' match (common.ps1:5796) and the hedged wording 'it may be the coordinator's own model' (5844) instead of asserting every model of that label is the coordinator's own model.

D6: an open tool call suspends the stall cut for at most max(3 x StallSec, 1800 s) (Wait-EngineProcess tool-cap, ~8555-8618; wording ~4450), so a never-completing tool call can no longer keep the stall cut suspended for the whole turn; confirmed against the prior-consultation read and the D6 decision.
Same fix as F30-3: the carry is bounded at 1 MiB and only new bytes are scanned (common.ps1:8416-8477), so an unbounded partial line cannot grow memory/CPU per tick.

D13: the hook's pointer line prints the full script path via Join-Path $PSScriptRoot (hook.ps1:113-115) and -Explain replaces ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} with the plugin directory (consult.ps1:887-891), so a host that substitutes nothing still gets a runnable command.

D14: every CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_* hook is read through Get-TestHookValue, which returns '' unless CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_MODE=1 (common.ps1:280-287) and ignored hooks are warned once; residual narrow risk (TEST_MODE itself propagating to children, requiring a double opt-in) noted in the reply, not filed.
D15: the -Explain path writes through Console.OpenStandardOutput inside try/finally with .Dispose() (consult.ps1:894-898), so the stream handle is released.

Telemetry privacy: open <codex home>/telemetry-spool/<date>.ndjson and confirm exactly one event per commit whose details carry only the allowlisted keys (engine, provider, model, purpose, outcome, wall_seconds, tokens{in,cached,out}, findings{blocker,major,minor,note}, structured, format_retry, denial_retry, timeout_continue, panel_size, ps_version, os, bridge_version), tags=[engine,provider], title an outcome enum, instance_id a 64-hex string - and no path, task slug, prompt text, thread id, user name or machine name in clear.

Coordinator identity: the run prints the Format-CoordinatorText line with host, host_by (markers|path|none) and source; if CODEX_CONSULT_COORDINATOR names no roster entry confirm '(not in the roster - no reviewer can match it)' appears and the run still proceeds (no exit 1), and if it is '#n' naming nothing confirm the unresolved warning rather than a refusal.

Confirmed kill: on a timeout the ledger records kill_confirmed; if false the outcome text reads '(kill not confirmed: <why>; pid <n> may still run)' and NO continuation turn runs; on Windows confirm taskkill /T /F exit 0 and an empty survivors list.

Health retry wording: if a machine-health update fails, the ledger warning names the actual cause (not a hardcoded 'lock timeout'), the in-lock retry is a single ~1 s attempt and the after-lock retry runs; check the console summary for the final cause (finding #1).

Kick protocol: run -Kick -Member NN against a live member and confirm the caller waits for its own id and exits 0 ('stopped' or 'late') or 3 (no ack within 10 s) with no .consult.kick-* or .ack left behind; a second concurrent kicker joins the same id and both reach a terminal result.

Bounded reader and tool cap: a normal run shows no oversized_lines warning, and a long silent tool call is not cut before max(3 x StallSec, 1800 s) - a cut names the open-tool duration rather than a premature stall.
Exit codes: exit 0 only when the reply is usable and (for a panel) all seated members are usable; exit 5 for a -Require refusal with nothing started; exit 3 for an unacknowledged kick.

-Complain fidelity: run -Complain '<text>' without -Yes, confirm the pretty JSON shown matches the bytes posted on the immediate send, and if it falls back to the spool confirm the spooled line carries the same field values (finding #5).
